Each tensor of two basis vectors is killed by a high enough power of the diagonal $e$: expanding $(e\otimes1+1\otimes e)^N$, every term vanishes once $N>i+j$. Hence $e$ acts locally nilpotently on $X$.

If $X$ were finitely generated over $U(\mathfrak g)$, its weight decomposition and local $e$-finiteness would put it in $\mathcal O$. F2 then implies it is finitely generated over $U(\mathfrak n^-)=\mathbb C[f]$, hence over $\mathbb C[x+y]$ in the displayed model.

But $\mathbb C[x,y]/(x+y)\mathbb C[x,y]\cong\mathbb C[x]$ is infinite dimensional over $\mathbb C$. A module generated by $r<\infty$ elements over $\mathbb C[x+y]$ has quotient by $x+y$ generated by their $r$ images over $\mathbb C$, so that quotient has dimension at most $r$. This proves that $X$ is not finitely generated and therefore is not in $\mathcal O$, although each factor is cyclic with locally nilpotent $e$ and is a weight module.
